data.body: Final rebar-debug report. Problem: close reran the completion verifier even when the ticket already held a certified PASS at the identical resolved ref. Proven root cause: src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py unconditionally entered verify_with_auto_resume, and src/rebar/_commands/close_autoresume.py called the provider before consulting the existing signed completion op-cert. Proof: an ephemeral tracker with a certified same-ref PASS plus a counting provider spy closed only after one redundant provider call on pre-fix main. Test: tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_completion_attestation_reuse.py was held out from the fixer, observed RED, then GREEN across same-ref reuse and nine ineligible controls; deleting the reuse dispatch restored exact-defect RED, and restoring it returned GREEN. Fix: _reusable_attested_pass now accepts only a cryptographically verified PASS whose authenticated explicit SHA, signed head, material fingerprint, ticket lifecycle, and close ref all remain current; eligible close returns zero provider calls, while malformed, stale, changed-ref, reopened, FAIL, and unverifiable records fall through to fresh verification. Scope and safety: the shared close path covers CLI, public library, and MCP; no dependency or test weakening; 81 focused tests, lint, typecheck, complexity, module-size, and diff checks passed. Siblings: standalone verify-completion remains intentionally render-only; intra-run insufficiency auto-resume remains distinct and unchanged. Residual advisory disposition: accepted. reuse_provenance is diagnostic in-memory metadata while the durable replacement op-cert already signs runner=reused/model; directly asserting all metadata fields or the redundant signed-SHA mismatch sub-branch would strengthen implementation-detail coverage but is not required for the observable zero-provider contractual guarantee. Replication: the original certified same-ref close now completes without invoking the provider.
